niche.diet: rondo dung, carcass leavings, pan_de_humus fungal growths, detritus

chains.trait: Membranous wings folded under rigid fore-shields
links: Reduces metabolic cost for cave transit

skill.effect: The creature launches forward through the thick air, easily clearing a short vertical drop. You watch it swiftly leap over the gap and land securely above.

journal.en: Wings like paper. The air is thick enough to swim.

plausibility.summary: At ~4.2 cm and ~0.8 g the beast sits in small-beetle mass class where powered and burst flight is routine on Earth; 1.6 bar air raises air density ~1.58×, which increases lift per wing area at low Reynolds number and favours short hops over sustained flight—matching a cave detritivore that only needs to cross vertical gaps when carrion or dung patches appear. Rigid fore-shields (elytra analogues) protect folded wings from abrasion and condensation on basalt in lava tubes (F9); episodic bonanzas (waterfall-cave carcass rains) can select retained flight even in otherwise dark caves, as with carrion-oriented insects elsewhere rather than full troglobitic wing loss.

Rigid fore-shields (elytra analogues) protect folded wings from abrasion and condensation on basalt in lava tubes (F9); episodic bonanzas (waterfall-cave carcass rains) can select retained flight even in otherwise dark caves, as with carrion-oriented insects elsewhere rather than full troglobitic wing loss.

analogues.organism: Scarab dung beetles (e.g. Scarabaeinae): elytra covering hind wings, burst flight to resources; cave cockroaches and cave crickets (Rhaphidophoridae) with partially retained jumping/gliding escape flight in hypogean habitats.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

skill.effect: The creature strongly follows the dung scent through the air, causing hidden carcass fragments to become visible. You can now clearly see the scattered remains it has uncovered.

chains.weakness: Sudden bright light blinds and freezes it
observe: Moving by touch in total dark

journal.en: It reads the dark. Scent hangs longer where the wind sleeps.

plausibility.summary: Deep cave and nocturnal activity cap useful vision; chemoreception and mechanoreception on antennae locate dung, carcass leavings, and fungal patches in still, humid tube air. Molecular diffusion ~0.6× Earth (F16/D18) lengthens odour persistence in stagnant pockets, so long antennae sampling a larger volume per sweep are favoured over large compound eyes; recessed eyes fit stygobiont-style regression without total blindness if animals occasionally leave to cave mouths or follow moisture drafts.
fixes: Deep cave and nocturnal activity cap useful vision; chemoreception and mechanoreception on antennae locate dung, carcass leavings, and fungal patches in still, humid tube air. analogues.organism: Cave crickets and troglobitic beetles (reduced eyes, elongated antennae); ants and many coprophages where antennae are primary chemosensory organs.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Six jointed legs and chitinous carapace
links: Exoskeleton bears load instead of muscle
Six legs distribute stress on wet basalt

skill.effect: The creature scales the sheer rock face with steady grace, using its hooked feet to grip the stone. You watch it steadily ascend the vertical wall without slipping.

chains.weakness: Vulnerable when flipped on open ground

journal.en: Six points of contact. The heavy air keeps them low.

plausibility.summary: Replace “buoyant drag” with “higher drag and lower terminal velocity in 1.6 bar air stabilise drops from the ceiling and short glides”; keep six legs and carapace as stated.
fixes: Replace “buoyant drag” with “higher drag and lower terminal velocity in 1.6 bar air stabilise drops from the ceiling and short glides”; keep six legs and carapace as stated.

analogues.organism: Cave-adapted cockroaches and cave crickets: six legs, hooked tarsi on slick rock; terrestrial isopods and millipedes are detritivore analogues but hexapody is the standard insect-grade fix for this size on rubble.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Gut symbionts for fibrous waste processing
links: Fungal symbionts break down tough cellulose
Gut processes rondo dung and carcass bits

skill.effect: The creature devours the waste matter in a short while, leaving behind scattered bone and chitin fragments. You see the useful scraps remain on the ground for collection.

journal.en: They turn waste to wealth. One gut, many secrets.

plausibility.summary: If “gut pulsing with fungal glow” is literal bioluminescence inside the gut, mark highly speculative—chemiluminescence in gut symbionts is rare; safer as observer confusion with phosphorescent foxfire on pan_de_humus outside the body, or drop the glow.
fixes: If “gut pulsing with fungal glow” is literal bioluminescence inside the gut, mark highly speculative—chemiluminescence in gut symbionts is rare; safer as observer confusion with phosphorescent foxfire on pan_de_humus outside the body, or drop the glow.

analogues.organism: Dung beetles and coprophagic fly larvae with rich gut microbiomes; termites and ruminants for fibrolytic symbiosis; pill-woodlice and terrestrial isopods for detritus recycling (less specialized but same niche logic).

body_plan.origin: convergent arthropod morphology from seed-lineage polysaccharide cuticle

temperament: skittish, fast crawler, slow flyer, clusters around food
moments: When a carcass drifts down the waterfall cave shaft, hundreds drop from the ceiling like rain, their wings humming in the damp air as they form a living, chittering carpet over the meat.

journal.en: They fall when meat falls. The cave floor is a feast, if you know how to listen.
Six legs, no eyes, all stomach. They turn waste to wealth in the dark.
